W1_constant_boundary_is_trivial_rep.claim: a|_dD = const  <=>  the boundary datum lies in the trivial rep (j = 0)
W1_constant_boundary_is_trivial_rep.reading: a function on the circle decomposes into Fourier modes; the constant functions are exactly the rotation-invariant (m = 0, hence j = 0) part. So AEG's hypothesis 'a|_dD = c is constant' is the hypothesis 'the seam label is trivial'.
W1_constant_boundary_is_trivial_rep.status: standard consequence (Fourier decomposition on the circle)

W2_seam_label_table.reading: the seam label j decides *both* which helicity combinations exist and whether the weight depends on theta at all: j = 0 gives a theta-independent weight (flat distribution), transverse j = 1 gives ±(1±cos)/2. V4 measured that the physical weight varies by a factor 25/13 across one fibre, so the physical seam cannot be the scalar (j = 0) one.

W3_a3_versus_v4.aeg_side: A3: on {a != 0}, u = log|a|/|lambda| has |du| = 1, so the level sets are equidistants; a constant boundary value forces u = k -+ d_g(., dD), which is not smooth inside. There is no internal (transverse) degree of freedom.
W3_a3_versus_v4.conclusion: A3's 'no regular constant-boundary cap' and V4's 'no weight from the interface value' are the same deficiency: the interface has only one number, so there is nowhere for the angular data to live.
W3_a3_versus_v4.physics_side: V4: the weight is a function on the fibre; a colimit gluing collapses the fibre to a point. V5: the weight needs a rep space and a rotation.
W3_a3_versus_v4.the_bridge: a scalar transported along the seam carries no theta: moving along the seam changes nothing transverse, so any weight built from it is constant in theta. The weight that physics needs IS theta-dependent, so it cannot come from the scalar sector.

W4_x4_tension_resolved_by_W1.previous_tension: V6 §X4: capping a seam contributes dim V_e (a number) while Thm 10.12 says a constant-boundary cap is impossible.
W4_x4_tension_resolved_by_W1.resolution_by_W1: W1 identifies 'constant boundary' with 'trivial label j = 0'. So both statements are about the *same* case: at j = 0 the algebraic contraction is the number 1 = dim V_e, while the analytic realisation is obstructed (A3). They are two layers of one label, not two claims about different labels.
W4_x4_tension_resolved_by_W1.what_would_upgrade_it: exhibit an AEG interface whose label is j != 0 and show that the capping obstruction does not apply to it (a j != 0 seam cannot be capped by the vacuum at all, only paired)

limitations: W2's j=1 rows reuse the conventions of ../pants-v5-labels/ without re-deriving them
W3 and W4 are structural proposals, not theorems; W4's upgrade needs a j != 0 AEG interface
nothing here touches the AEG repository; the translation is not yet a statement in the paper
